newsitem.title: UK: FTSE Intl launches new pan-European stock index.
newsitem.headline: FTSE Intl launches new pan-European stock index.

text.p: FTSE International said on Thursday it had launched a new pan-European stock index in co-operation with the Amsterdam Exchanges, aimed at supporting the growing market for pan-European equities trading.

Under the terms of the deal, FTSE International -- which manages the major UK stock indexes -- will operate Amsterdam's Eurotop 100 index and will also introduce a complementary and wider-based European index called the FTSE Eurotop 300.

Amsterdam, which currently lists futures and options on the FTSE Eurotop 100, will also list the FTSE Eurotop 300 for options trading. Talks are underway with LIFFE, the London futures and options exchange, to also trade derivates on the two indices.

Mark Makepeace, managing director of FTSE International, said: "The integration of the European markets has begun and this process will certainly speed up as we move close to the introduction of the Euro in 1999."

"We have seen a significant increase in demand for pan-European index-linked products in the OTC (over-the-counter) market this year," Makepeace said. "These indices will meet this demand and be the basis for exchange-traded derivaties in the run-up to EMU."

Amsterdam restructured the Eurotop 100 in April to reflect the market capitalisation of the major European countries. Options on the index have traded in Amsterdam since 1991 and dollar-denominated futures and options trade on Comex and Amex in the United States.
FTSE International said the FTSE Eurotop 300 represented the largest 300 companies in Europe, covering 13 countries and providing exposure to around 65 percent of total market capitalisation.
It would cover companies included in existing indexes such as the FTSE 100, DAX 30 and CAC 40. Real-time foreign exchange and share price data to calculate the indexes will be supplied by Reuters.

George Moeller, chief executive and president of Amsterdam Exchanges, said: "The combination of Amsterdam Exchanges' trading experience and FTSE International's index knowledge will provide the platform for us to succeed in creating the first truly liquid market for trading European index derivatives."
"The increasing volumes of the existing U.S. listings indicate that there is a future for further listings in Europe."
Trading volume in the Eurotop 100 reached an average daily 31.7 million ECU in the first quarter of 1997, compared with 19.5 million through 1996.
